error_message: IndexError: list index out of range when writing patched TMX
root_cause: ET.tostring(root, encoding='UTF-8') was assumed to emit an XML declaration that could be split off with .split(b'?>\n',1)[1]; it did not emit one in that form, so index [1] was out of range.
fix: Use ET.tostring(root, encoding='utf-8', xml_declaration=False) and prepend the desired b'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n' literal. Note ET emits single-quoted declarations, which is why the literal is needed to byte-match the original files.

error_message: [gold priors] eflomal.calculate_priors failed for en: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
root_cause: A gold record (sentence_id 0, 'lefe texto' <-> 'Preface') carries links [[0,1],[1,2],[0,0],[1,0]] while the stored target has only 1 token, so j=1 and j=2 are out of bounds. eflomal.calculate_priors raises on the first out-of-bounds link, and its own error path is buggy -- `raise ValueError('Invalid input on line %d' % lineno + 1)` evaluates as (str % int) + int, so a TypeError masks the real 'alignment out of bounds' message. Because the bad record was first in the list, ALL 54 gold records were silently discarded (run_giza_improved catches the exception and prints '[gold priors] skipped').
fix: _pharaoh() now takes optional n_src/n_tgt and drops links pointing past either token list, returning (pharaoh_string, dropped_count). append_gold_priors() passes the token counts, logs which sentence_id had out-of-bounds links, and warns that those rows are stale and need re-annotation. Verified: all 54 gold records now yield 364 LEX / 13 HMMF / 14 HMMR / 261 FERF / 271 FERR priors.

error_message: apkg_image_sync.py read Anki image fields by hardcoded ordinal (img=14, src=15, gif=19, gif_src=20); ordinal 14 is IntransitiveCu in the current notetype
root_cause: IMAGE_NOTETYPES hardcoded field positions captured before AnkiMaker3 v3 inserted the per-VerbType fields (Transitive..State, ords 11-18). That pushed the image fields from 14/15/19/20 to 19/20/24/25, so the sync silently read verb-type text as image URLs. The second notetype's offsets (Globasa lexi SabziFruta) were wrong too.
fix: Resolve field ordinals from the apkg's own `fields` table by NAME (Imajelinku, ImajeAsel, DuayumImaje, DuayumImajeAsel, Faleanimalinku, Faleanimaasel). Same rule as word-list.csv: use header names, never positions. Verified against the live deck: ntid 1761931224511 -> 19/20/22/23/24/25, ntid 1762076920706 -> 8/9/11/12.

error_message: apkg_image_sync re-imported 4 images the store already had, under their pre-rename titles
root_cause: resolve_commons_images.py adopts the canonical title when the MediaWiki API follows a file redirect, but discarded the old one. The Anki deck still holds the pre-rename URL, so the identity check saw a different file and adopted the same picture twice (e.g. Europe-Bosnia_and_Herzegovina.svg vs Map_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina_in_Europe.svg).
fix: Record the former title in the image's `aka` list on rename, and add images_store.image_keys() returning canonical + former identities. apkg_image_sync matches against that set. Round-trip now reports 0 new images.

error_message: New records for yamxey/flura/mamoyen vanished after save_images(); the JSONL never contained them
root_cause: save_images dropped any record with no images via `if not all_images(rec) and is_illustratable(rec) and len(rec) <= 2`. A hypernym illustrated entirely by its hyponyms owns no image, so a derive-only record matched the drop condition and was silently discarded. The in-memory dict still looked right, which is why the first verification pass missed it -- it printed the mapping rather than reloading the file.
fix: Extracted is_empty_record(): a record survives if it has images, any sense with a `derive` spec, an illustratable=false marker, or any hand-added key on the record or a sense. Only a bare {word, senses} with plain empty senses is dropped. Verified by reloading from disk rather than trusting the in-memory mapping.

error_message: Adding a sense in the image curator was a placebo: the POST reported ok, the sense never persisted (reported on salamandra)
root_cause: is_empty_record dropped any record with no images. A word with no pictures that gains a freshly-created empty sense is exactly that, so save_images discarded it; the UI then re-read the store and honestly showed nothing. Same root cause as bug-186 (derive-only records) -- that was patched by special-casing `derive` instead of fixing the rule.
fix: is_empty_record now returns True only for a bare {word, senses:[]} with no hand-set keys. Any sense at all is intent, as is any unrecognised key on the record. Deleting the last sense still decays the record and cleans it up.

error_message: Editing a sense label in the image curator kicks you out of the field the moment you click into it
root_cause: The .sense container's click handler ran renderSenses(), which rebuilds the whole sense list. Clicking the label input bubbles up to that handler, so the input you just clicked into was destroyed and replaced mid-click.
fix: Selecting a sense no longer rebuilds the DOM: setActive(i) just toggles the .active class on the existing elements. The label input and PoS select also set the active sense on focus, and their change handlers return early when the value is unchanged, so tabbing through a field no longer triggers a save-and-rebuild.

error_message: A fully-curated word (salamandra) could no longer be opened in the image curator
root_cause: /api/images/words dropped any word with no unillustrated PoS before applying the search filter, and the queue is the only way to open a word. So finishing a word made it unreachable -- you could not revisit it to fix, reorder or extend the curation.
fix: The search filter is applied first and a non-empty query bypasses the done-filter entirely: typing a word's name is a request for that word, finished or not. The unfiltered queue still lists only outstanding work.

error_message: Recurring: words whose gloss carries a plain parenthetical after the colon were split into extra part-of-speech slots in the Anki deck (e.g. dento 'that; that one', keto 'what, which; what, which one', lil 'minorly, a little; minorly, a little bit')
root_cause: _parseAnnotatedEnglish always ran _expand_gloss_context, which turns a gloss with a plain (non-italic) parenthetical into TWO readings -- compact and verbose ('ace (card)' -> 'ace', 'ace card'). That expansion exists for sense matching: extending glosses into more languages via Wiktionary and Apertium. But AnkiMaker3 lays each ParsedGloss into a slot of its own, so one gloss consumed two, doubling the text in a slot and silently dropping the parentheses where only the verbose reading survived ('be on top of' for 'be on top (of)').
fix: Threaded an expand_context flag through _parseAnnotatedEnglish. parseEntry -- used only by the Anki makers, which are slot-based -- defaults it to False, so a parenthetical stays intact in one slot. parseWordEntry keeps expanding, so the dictionary, Wiktionary extension and Apertium paths are untouched. 568 of 8879 exported rows corrected.

error_message: apkg_image_sync.py re-added an image the store already had, duplicating it on colo and coloya
root_cause: The already-present check misses images whose store entry is still status:'unresolved' (no direct_url). The deck field then holds the Special:FilePath form while the store entry has only `file`, and the two do not compare equal, so the image is appended as a second copy of itself.
fix: Not fixed -- reverted with git checkout. The sync runs deck -> store, which is the wrong direction while the curated store supersedes the deck; do not run it after pushing the store into the apkg.

error_message: update_vocab_deck.py reported 425-675 notes updated on every run even when nothing had changed; the only field written was <tags>
root_cause: Tags were compared as ordered lists. Anki stores them in its own canonical (case-insensitive alphabetical) order, while AnkiList.csv carries the wordlist's order, so every note with two or more tags looked changed on every run and got re-stamped.
fix: Compare as case-insensitive sets, which is Anki's actual tag semantics. A re-run against an already-current deck now reports 0 updates.

error_message: Word viewer: translation table overlaps the etymology column (kroa)
root_cause: '.entry-grid' used 'grid-template-columns: 1fr auto'; the auto track sized to the etymology table's max-content (~505px of a 900px content box), so the 1fr track fell to ~355px -- below the translation table's ~422px min-content. With '.entry-col-left { min-width: 0 }' the table could not shrink and overflowed its column, painting over the etymology.
fix: Capped the sidebar with '.entry-col-right { max-width: 20rem }' so the etymology can never starve the left track; added 'overflow-x: auto' to .trans-section so an unusually wide table (2 languages + type column + images) scrolls inside its own column instead of overlapping; 'overflow-wrap: break-word' on .etym-val; raised the stacking breakpoint from 600px to 48rem.

error_message: Translation aide: 'un' toggle chip appears on 'kroa' but not on 'zway' in "The frog eats the fly." -> "kroa[un] nun yam zway▾"
root_cause: renderOutput() uses a mutually exclusive if/else-if chain: branch A (polysemy dropdown, line 594) precedes branch B (un toggle, line 600). Any noun that follows a suppressed English article AND has >1 bilingual alternative renders only the polysemy dropdown, so its article control is silently dropped. 'zway' is polysemous, 'kroa' is not.
fix: Restructured renderOutput() so the marker chips are appended to the token span before the word body, independently of the if/else-if chain that picks the body (polysemy dropdown / article selector / plain text). The polysemy styling moved off the outer .token onto an inner span so the chip does not inherit its underline, and the dropdown now mounts on closest('.token'), which is the element CSS already gives position: relative.

error_message: Translation aide: "the un is in an awkward spot. It should be before a noun, not after" (rendered as "kroa[un] nun yam zway")
root_cause: renderOutput() branch B set span.textContent = displayText first and then appended the un toggle, so the chip landed after the noun -- but Globasa word order puts 'un' before its noun ('un kroa'), so the chip contradicted the text it would insert.
fix: Append the toggle first, then the noun as a text node (mirrors branch C's article-selector for glb-eng); .un-toggle margin-left: 0.2em -> margin-right: 0.2em.

error_message: Transliterators emit phonotactically illegal Globasa forms without flagging them
root_cause: They perform grapheme mapping only, with no phonotactic validation. turkishToGlobasa('minnet')->'minnet' keeps a geminate (0 of 3183 roots) and final -t (1 of 3183); pinyinToGlobasa('renqing')->'rencing' ends in -g, outside the legal coda set {n,m,l,r,s,y,f,x,w}.
fix: NOT APPLIED - reported. Add a validator: legal codas n/m/l/r/s/y/f/x/w or vowel; no final clusters; no geminates; initial clusters limited to obstruent+{r,l,w,y}; medial clusters checked against attested inventory.

error_message: vietnameseToGlobasa does not convert the vowel o-horn (u+01A1)

error_message: Lesson 11: 12 ticked segments (Engli, Espani, Nipon, ... Brazil) were never exported from /splits
root_cause: SPLIT_NAME_RE allowed only lowercase ([a-z]+(_[a-z]+)*), so capitalised proper nouns were refused as 'names that cannot be filenames'. The /audio route had the same lowercase-only check, so Engli.ogg and suffix clips like -sa.ogg would not play in the dictionary either. Also: one failing ffmpeg call aborted the whole export with a 500.
fix: SPLIT_NAME_RE = -?[A-Za-z]+(?:_[A-Za-z]+)*, reused by /audio. Export collects per-clip ffmpeg failures in 'failed' and carries on.

error_message: llama-server: warning: no usable GPU found, --gpu-layers option will be ignored; about 10 tokens/s
root_cause: The user's shell finds Homebrew's llama.cpp 8260 first, a CPU-only build with no Vulkan or CUDA backend and only SSE3/SSSE3 reported. /usr/bin/llama-server (8262) is a Vulkan build, but its backends are in /usr/lib where it does not search unless the working directory is /usr/lib. The earlier 27B slowness was also CPU only.

error_message: Flash 9B: loga 'to say, to tell' scored 0.393 at H and 0.002 at lowercase a; 'to recite' won that whole option order

fix: MAX_OPTIONS 25 so only A-Z are used, long lists run in groups; default 4 shuffles from the --rotate test. loga 'to say, to tell' then won all 12 usages.

error_message: Replaying sense_review_queue.py --tag=flash9b from a copied cache hit cache misses (ConnectionRefused on /apply-template) although the run had finished
root_cause: select_words samples from words with vetted rows and the vetting log grew after the run, so the current log can select different words and prompts, which miss the cache keyed on prompt text. Script unchanged; the report goes only to stdout, so it is lost unless captured.
fix: No code change. Replayed in a scratch directory with symlinked inputs and sense_vetting.jsonl truncated to verdicts up to 18:21; scores TSV came out byte-identical. Later cutoffs (18:33 on) still missed.

error_message: Perimetric complexity about 4x too high (DejaVu Sans 277)
root_cause: Cauchy-Crofton perimeter over four directions used pi/4 instead of pi/8, doubling the perimeter
fix: Use pi/8; DejaVu Sans now 69, in the expected range for sans letters

root_cause: Cao & Zhai arc formula takes the angle in radians; I passed degrees
fix: Convert sweep to radians; now 129-260 ms/letter

error_message: First provisional consonants retraced their own line on ka, fe, ha, ji (interior angle under 25 degrees)
root_cause: Signs ending near 225 degrees reverse straight back along an up-right connector; a low time cost does not mean a readable join
fix: Reassigned signs so end headings avoid about 195-265 degrees; reduced arc sweeps; joint check kept in metrics script

error_message: in rendered as a blob at writing size
root_cause: n hook 0.3 units with a full 180 degree turn was too tight after a vowel

error_message: Background wait loop never finished; later pkill killed its own shell (exit 144)
root_cause: pgrep -f / pkill -f pattern matched the waiting command's own command line
fix: Wait on PIDs (wait/kill by PID) or use a pattern the waiter's command line cannot contain, e.g. pgrep -f '[s]horthand_optimizer'

error_message: Search quality collapsed (letters touching in 20% of words, 9 loops) after adding the similar-sign rule
root_cause: 'Similar' counted line directions 45 degrees apart and line sizes, which Callendar treats as safe; with simple shapes nearly every letter pair became 'similar', so an unavoidable penalty drove the search into worse joins
fix: Restrict similarity to fragile distinctions (circle direction, 45-degree loop/semicircle rotation, curved size), lower SIMILAR_MS to 100; verified by rerunning old rules on the new fast code (no regression)

error_message: NameError: return_y not defined in contacts() after adding window_metrics
root_cause: contacts() and contacts_fast() end with identical lines; a str.replace hit the first function
fix: Moved the vertical-range return into contacts_fast only; when editing near-duplicate code, anchor replacements inside the target function

error_message: `from update_vocab_deck import COLUMNS` (to reuse its column list) ran the whole script and rewrote Globasa__Vocabulary.apkg, overwriting its .bak
root_cause: Project scripts have no __main__ guard by convention; importing one executes it, including its file writes
fix: Restored the apkg from .bak (byte-identical). Read constants from scripts with ast/text slicing or exec of an isolated section on a scratch collection, never import

error_message: emphasize_main_gloss dropped the last gloss of a row when fronting an override (kone lost 'be acquainted with', kinmyetu lost 'despise')
root_cause: Separator list for the non-core glosses was sliced with [-len(tail):] from a filtered list one shorter than the tail, so zip() stopped early
fix: Emit each non-core gloss with the separator that preceded it in the original (seps[i-1], ',' for index 0); test asserts gloss count is preserved

error_message: Word Selector: Japanese 基質 not clustered with Mandarin 基质/Korean 기질 (matrix); proposals missing below top 4 clusters
root_cause: Sino-xenic readings (kixitsu ~ jiji) exceed the 0.30 phonetic threshold under average linkage (0.317); pipeline capped proposals at TOP_CLUSTERS=4
fix: Added sino_distance (MC initial correspondences, optional Japanese -tsu/-ku coda reduction, Korean -l->t, cheap coda-stop gaps) gated by _sino_ok (one side Han, equal morpheme count, positional shared char if both Han) + shared-Han-character link; proposals for all clusters

error_message: SyntaxError: sense_key = translation.get('sense') or  (JSONL parser non-English.py line 187)
root_cause: Python heredoc replacement string contained '' inside a triple-quoted ''' literal, which swallowed the empty-string literal
fix: Fixed the line with Edit to `or ''`; use the Edit tool for replacements containing quotes

root_cause: build_reverse post-pass never completed: the reverse sub-db had 0 entries

error_message: ValueError: too many values to unpack in contrasts._side_has
root_cause: find()'s new pivot parameter was shadowed by the loop variable over edition pivot words
fix: Renamed the loop variable to pw

error_message: IndexError: list index out of range in precedent.lookup (follow layer)
root_cause: A class pattern's follow Counter can be empty or zeroed by leave-one-out subtraction (Globasa took none of the members' letters)
fix: Use positive counts (+Counter) and skip empty ones

error_message: User: Japanese kishitsu (基質) missing from the matrix sources when it was found before
root_cause: Japanese 基質 is in no English Wiktionary translation table, has no English-Wiktionary entry, and is not the Wikidata label for Q1463013 (石基); it only appears when the concept supplies it (e.g. a ja seed), so a concept with only a cmn seed lost it
fix: pipeline.add_han_cognates: after gathering, add same-Han-spelling cognates in missing Sinosphere languages when attested (ja: Japanese Wiktionary or English Wiktionary entry; cmn: English Wiktionary zh entry; ko/vi: hanja/chữ Hán tables); compounds only; Korean/Vietnamese homographs pass on only spellings another language confirms; flagged 'check the meaning'

error_message: Persian words transliterated from the Classical/Dari romanization (kitāb, afsāna) instead of the Iranian one LexiliAsel uses (ketab, afsane); 726/1679 Persian etymons had no input at all
root_cause: lookup() returned entry romanizations in dump order (Classical first) and every caller takes [0]; it ignored the tr= romanizations of translation tables, the only reading for most Persian words without an entry
fix: lookup() ranks Persian romanizations Iranian first (â; then no macrons) and falls back to table_romans() (translation-table tr=, majority) when entries give none; roman_from says which. Also removed translit PERSIAN iyV->iV (râdiyo/bâmiye: LexiliAsel keeps radiyo/bamiye)

error_message: Native Korean 독 'jar' shown with historical Han 毒 / 獨 (단지 'jar' with 但只 / 團地)
root_cause: sinosphere's hanja table lists every Sino homograph of a Hangul spelling; display_han showed all spellings when none was shared with the cluster
fix: display_han shows only spellings another Sinosphere word of the cluster/concept shares; the rest are 'Han homographs, unconfirmed' in the sources table only

error_message: de:Topf 'kleines Gefäß' reported as bridging to no English table when en:pot was also a concept sense
root_cause: english_view deduplicated bridge rows against the concept's existing English rows before deciding bridged/unbridged
fix: collect matches first (a match already present still counts as a bridge), dedupe only when appending

error_message: User: kijitu should still be favoured for matrix (geology); proposals were gijil, jijitu, kijitu
root_cause: (1) 7a31746 coda_stats counted roots whose Han spelling merely ends in an MC -t character (pilpil, tofa) as 'dropped', -tu share 4/15; (2) 5c93d36 sino_align training split the j/k/g initial column so no language was followed >=0.6 (ja 4/8), the precedent disappeared and gijil/jijit stopped paying a departure
fix: coda_stats requires two surface reflexes (not cmn, not the reading); precedent.lookup gains a last letter-level fallback (letter_model) for >=3-language columns with >=2*MIN_COUNT roots; bisected with git archive copies + symlinked data in the scratchpad

error_message: lmdb.ReadonlyError: mdb_dbi_open: Permission denied / lookups 404 after a failed first start
root_cause: build_db wrote straight into WordViewerLMDB; a crash (missing input) left an empty or partial DB that later starts opened as if built
fix: build into WordViewerLMDB.building and os.replace when complete; _open_built_db rebuilds a DB with missing sub-dbs or an empty wordlist

root_cause: serve_font used send_file(os.path.join(...)); no 404 and no '..' guard

error_message: menalariExtension.tsv reorders senses/translations on every rebuild

fix: sorted() in both joins; two runs with different seeds now byte-identical

error_message: vetted sense abece/alphabetize missing from the extension
root_cause: Tier cell 'v ' (trailing space) failed the builder's tier in ('v','e') test
fix: export strips Tier/App? whitespace and reports it; unknown tiers (sl) kept and reported

error_message: sense_vetter.py unusable on a fresh clone: reads untracked 'GLB_ENG_WiktionarySenses (copy).xlsx'; its 988 verdicts never reached vetted_senses.tsv or the extension
root_cause: vetter read a hand-made spreadsheet snapshot and kept its verdicts in an untracked, separate jsonl keyed only by (word,label)
fix: sense_rows.py generates the senses; log entries carry [eng,pos,vt] keys (migrated); log tracked and overlaid by vetted_senses.load_rows(); setup.sh --vetter builds WiktionaryLMDB_senses

error_message: Word Selector on a fresh clone: empty clusters with errors: [], /api/senses and /api/entry 500; concept index builder hardcodes /media dump path; parts/etym_reverse never built
root_cause: WiktionaryLMDB_concepts and caches were built ad hoc on one machine; no setup step; server did not check for the index
